Main.sentence: John Sidney McCain III (August 29, 1936 – August 25, 2018) was an American statesman  and ___E:naval U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy)___ officer who represented ___E:Arizona U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona)___ in the ___E:United States Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress)___ for over 35 years, first as a ___E:U.S. representative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ from 1983 to 1987, then as a ___E:U.S. senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ from 1987 until his death in 2018. A member of the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ , he was the party's nominee in the ___E:2008 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

Born into the prominent ___E:McCain family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCain_family)___ in the ___E:Panama Canal Zone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_Canal_Zone)___ , McCain graduated from the ___E:U.S. Naval Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Naval_Academy)___ in 1958 and ___E:received a commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_military_career_of_John_McCain)___ in the U.S.

Navy. He became a ___E:naval aviator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_aviator_(United_States))___ and flew ___E:ground-attack aircraft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ground-attack_aircraft)___ from ___E:aircraft carriers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carrier)___ .
During the ___E:Vietnam War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War)___ , he almost died in the ___E:1967 USS Forrestal fire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_USS_Forrestal_fire)___ .

While on a bombing mission during ___E:Operation Rolling Thunder U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Rolling_Thunder)___ over ___E:Hanoi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanoi)___ in October 1967, McCain was shot down, seriously injured, and captured by the ___E:North Vietnamese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Vietnam)___ .

He was a ___E:prisoner of war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner_of_war)___ until 1973. McCain experienced episodes of ___E:torture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torture)___ and refused an out-of-sequence early ___E:release U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repatriation)___ .
He sustained wounds that left him with lifelong physical disabilities.
McCain retired from the Navy as a ___E:captain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(United_States_O-6))___ in 1981 and moved to Arizona.
In 1982, McCain was elected to the House of Representatives, where he served two terms.
Four years later, he was elected to the Senate, where he served six terms.

While generally adhering to conservative principles, McCain also gained a reputation as a "maverick" for his willingness to break from his party on certain issues, including ___E:LGBT rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_the_United_States)___ , ___E:gun regulations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_regulation)___ , and ___E:campaign finance reform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campaign_finance_reform_in_the_United_States)___ where his stances were more moderate than those of the party's base. McCain was investigated and largely exonerated in a political influence scandal of the 1980s as one of the ___E:Keating Five U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keating_Five)___ .

He then made regulating the ___E:financing of political campaigns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financing_of_political_campaigns)___ one of his signature concerns, which eventually resulted in the passage of the ___E:McCain–Feingold Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCain%E2%80%93Feingold_Act)___ in 2002. With ___E:Russ Feingold U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russ_Feingold)___ , McCain would receive the 1999 ___E:John F. Kennedy Profile in Courage Award U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Profile_in_Courage_Award)___ .
He was also known for his work in the 1990s to restore ___E:diplomatic relations with Vietnam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States%E2%80%93Vietnam_relations)___ .

McCain chaired the ___E:Senate Commerce Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_Commerce_Committee)___ from 1997 to 2001 and 2003 to 2005, where he opposed ___E:pork barrel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pork_barrel)___ spending and ___E:earmarks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earmark_(politics))___ .
He belonged to the bipartisan " ___E:Gang of 14 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gang_of_14)___ ", which played a key role in alleviating a crisis over judicial nominations.

McCain entered the race for the ___E:2000 Republican presidential nomination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain_2000_presidential_campaign)___ , but lost ___E:a heated primary season contest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries)___ to ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ .

He secured the ___E:2008 Republican presidential nomination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain_2008_presidential_campaign)___ , beating fellow candidates ___E:Mitt Romney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney)___ and ___E:Mike Huckabee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Huckabee)___ , though he lost the general election to ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ .

McCain subsequently adopted more orthodox conservative stances and attitudes and largely opposed actions of the ___E:Obama administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obama_administration)___ , especially with regard to foreign policy matters.
In 2015, he became Chairman of the ___E:Senate Armed Services Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_Armed_Services_Committee)___ .

He refused to support ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ in the ___E:2016 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election)___ and later became a vocal critic of the ___E:first Trump administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump)___ .

While McCain opposed the Obama-era ___E:Affordable Care Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act)___ (ACA), he cast the deciding vote against the ___E:American Health Care Act of 2017 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Health_Care_Act_of_2017)___ , which would have partially repealed the ACA. After being diagnosed with ___E:glioblastoma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glioblastoma)___ in 2017, he reduced his role in the Senate to focus on treatment, dying from the disease in 2018.

John Sidney McCain III was born on August 29, 1936, at ___E:Coco Solo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Solo)___ Naval Air Station in the ___E:Panama Canal Zone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_Canal_Zone)___ , to naval officer ___E:John S. McCain Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_S._McCain_Jr.)___ and ___E:Roberta Wright McCain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberta_McCain)___ .
He had an older sister, Sandy, and a younger brother, ___E:Joe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_McCain)___ .
At that time, the ___E:Panama Canal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_Canal)___ was under U.S. control.

His father and his paternal grandfather, ___E:John S. McCain Sr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_S._McCain_Sr.)___ , were also ___E:Naval Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Academy_(United_States))___ graduates and both became ___E:four-star admirals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four-star_admiral)___ in the ___E:United States Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy)___ .
The McCain family moved with their father as he took various naval postings in the United States and in the Pacific.
As a result, the younger McCain attended a total of about 20 schools.

In 1951, the family settled in ___E:Northern Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Virginia)___ , and McCain attended ___E:Episcopal High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_High_School_(Alexandria))___ , a private preparatory boarding school in ___E:Alexandria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandria,_Virginia)___ .

He excelled at ___E:wrestling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scholastic_wrestling)___ and graduated in 1954.   He referred to himself as an ___E:Episcopalian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_Church_(United_States))___ as recently as June 2007, after which date he said he came to identify as a ___E:Baptist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptist)___ .

Following in the footsteps of his father and grandfather, McCain entered the ___E:United States Naval Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Naval_Academy)___ , where he was a friend and informal leader for many of his classmates  and sometimes stood up for targets of ___E:bullying U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullying)___ .
He also fought as a lightweight ___E:boxer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing)___ .

He earned the nickname "John Wayne" "for his attitude and popularity with the opposite sex."  McCain did well in academic subjects that interested him, such as literature and history, but studied only enough to pass subjects that gave him difficulty, such as mathematics.

He came into conflict with higher-ranking personnel and did not always obey the rules. "He collected demerits the way some people collect stamps."  His ___E:class rank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_rank)___ (894 of 899) was not indicative of his intelligence nor his ___E:IQ U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence_quotient)___ , which had been tested to be 128 and 133.   McCain graduated in 1958.

___E:McCain began his early military career U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_military_career_of_John_McCain#Naval_training,_early_assignments,_first_marriage,_and_children)___ when he was commissioned as an ___E:ensign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ensign_(rank)#United_States)___ , and started two and a half years of training at ___E:Pensacola U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola,_Florida)___ to become a naval aviator.
While there, he earned a reputation as a man who partied.

He completed flight school in 1960, and became a naval pilot of ___E:ground-attack aircraft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ground-attack_aircraft)___ ; he was assigned to ___E:A-1 Skyraider U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Skyraider)___ squadrons  aboard the ___E:aircraft carriers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carrier)___ ___E:USS Intrepid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Intrepid_(CV-11))___ and ___E:USS Enterprise U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Enterprise_(CVN-65))___  in the ___E:Caribbean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea)___ and ___E:Mediterranean Seas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea)___ .

McCain began as a sub-par flier  who was at times careless and reckless;  during the early to mid-1960s, two of his flight missions crashed, and a third mission collided with power lines, but he received no major injuries.
His aviation skills improved over time,  and he was seen as a good pilot, albeit one who tended to " ___E:push the envelope U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_envelope)___ " in his flying.
On July 3, 1965, McCain was 28 when he married ___E:Carol Shepp U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carol_Shepp)___ , who had worked as a runway model and secretary.
McCain adopted her two young children, Douglas and Andrew.
He and Carol then had a daughter, Sidney.
The same year, he was a one-day champion on the game show ___E:Jeopardy! U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeopardy!)___

McCain requested a combat assignment,  and was assigned to the aircraft carrier ___E:USS Forrestal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Forrestal)___ flying ___E:A-4 Skyhawks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-4_Skyhawk)___ .  ___E:His combat duty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_military_career_of_John_McCain#Vietnam_operations)___ began in mid-1967, when Forrestal was assigned to a bombing campaign, ___E:Operation Rolling Thunder U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Rolling_Thunder)___ , during the ___E:Vietnam War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War)___ .

Stationed in the ___E:Gulf of Tonkin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Tonkin)___ , McCain and his fellow pilots became frustrated by micromanagement from Washington; he later wrote, "In all candor, we thought our civilian commanders were complete idiots who didn't have the least notion of what it took to win the war."

On July 29, 1967, McCain was a ___E:lieutenant commander U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_commander_(United_States))___ when he was near the center of the ___E:USS Forrestal fire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_USS_Forrestal_fire)___ .
He escaped from his burning jet and was trying to help another pilot escape when a bomb exploded;  McCain was struck in the legs and chest by fragments.
The ensuing fire killed 134 sailors.

With the Forrestal out of commission, McCain volunteered for assignment with the ___E:USS Oriskany U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Oriskany)___ , another carrier employed in Operation Rolling Thunder.

There, he was awarded the ___E:Navy Commendation Medal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_Commendation_Medal)___ and the ___E:Bronze Star Medal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_Star_Medal)___ for missions flown over North Vietnam.

McCain was taken ___E:prisoner of war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_military_career_of_John_McCain#Prisoner_of_war)___ on October 26, 1967. He was flying his 23rd bombing mission over ___E:North Vietnam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Vietnam)___ when his ___E:A-4E Skyhawk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-4E_Skyhawk)___ was shot down by a missile over ___E:Hanoi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanoi)___ .

McCain fractured both arms and a leg when he ejected from the aircraft,  and nearly drowned after he parachuted into ___E:Trúc Bạch Lake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tr%C3%BAc_B%E1%BA%A1ch_Lake)___ .

Some North Vietnamese pulled him ashore, then others crushed his shoulder with a rifle butt and bayoneted him.  McCain was then transported to Hanoi's main ___E:Hỏa Lò Prison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%E1%BB%8Fa_L%C3%B2_Prison)___ , nicknamed the "Hanoi Hilton".

Although McCain was seriously wounded and injured, his captors refused to treat him. They beat and ___E:interrogated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interrogated)___ him and he was given medical care only when the North Vietnamese discovered that his father was an admiral.
His status as a ___E:prisoner of war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner_of_war)___ (POW) made the front pages of major American newspapers.
McCain spent six weeks in the hospital, where he received marginal care. He had lost 50 pounds (23 kg), he was in a chest cast, and his gray hair had turned white.
McCain was sent to a different camp on the outskirts of Hanoi.

In December 1967, McCain was placed in a cell with two other Americans, who did not expect him to live more than a week.  In March 1968, McCain was placed in ___E:solitary confinement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solitary_confinement)___ , where he remained for two years.

In mid-1968, his father John S. McCain Jr. was named commander of all U.S. forces in the Vietnam theater, and the North Vietnamese offered McCain early release  because they wanted to appear merciful for propaganda purposes,  and also to show other POWs that elite prisoners were willing to be treated preferentially.

Such early release was prohibited by the POWs' interpretation of the military ___E:Code of Conduct U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_of_the_United_States_Fighting_Force)___ , which states in Article III: "I will accept neither parole nor special favors from the enemy."  McCain refused repatriation unless every man taken in before him was also released.
To prevent the enemy from using prisoners for propaganda, officers were to agree to be released in the order in which they were captured.
Beginning in August 1968, McCain was subjected to severe torture.
He was bound and beaten every two hours, and he was suffering from heat exhaustion and ___E:dysentery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dysentery)___ .
Further injuries brought McCain to "the point of suicide", but his preparations were interrupted by guards.
Eventually, McCain made an anti-U.S. propaganda "confession".
He had always felt that his statement was dishonorable, but as he later wrote: "I had learned what we all learned over there: every man has his breaking point.
I had reached mine."   Many U.S.
POWs were tortured and maltreated to extract "confessions" and propaganda statements;  virtually all eventually yielded something.
McCain received two to three beatings weekly because of his continued refusal to sign additional statements.
McCain refused to meet various anti-war groups seeking peace in Hanoi, wanting to give neither them nor the North Vietnamese a propaganda victory.
From late 1969, treatment of McCain and many of the other POWs became more tolerable,  while McCain continued to resist the camp authorities.

McCain and other prisoners cheered the ___E:U.S. "Christmas Bombing" campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Linebacker_II)___ of December 1972, viewing it as a forceful measure to push North Vietnam to terms.

McCain was a prisoner of war in North Vietnam for five and a half years, until his release on March 14, 1973, along with 108 other prisoners of war.  His wartime injuries left him permanently incapable of raising his arms above his head.  After the war, McCain, accompanied by his family, returned to the site on a few occasions.
McCain was reunited with his family when he ___E:returned U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_military_career_of_John_McCain#Return_to_United_States)___ to the United States.

His wife ___E:Carol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carol_McCain)___ had been severely injured by an automobile accident in December 1969. She was then four inches shorter, in a wheelchair or on crutches, and substantially heavier than when he had last seen her. As a returned POW, he became a celebrity of sorts.
McCain underwent treatment for his injuries that included months of ___E:physical therapy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_therapy)___ .

He attended the ___E:National War College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_War_College)___ at ___E:Fort McNair U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_McNair)___ in Washington, D.C., during 1973–1974.  He was rehabilitated by late 1974, and his flight status was reinstated.
In 1976, he became ___E:Commanding Officer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commanding_Officer)___ of a training squadron stationed in Florida.

He improved the unit's flight readiness and safety records,  and won the squadron its first-ever ___E:Meritorious Unit Commendation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meritorious_Unit_Commendation)___ .
During this period in Florida, he had extramarital affairs, and his marriage began to falter, about which he later stated: "The blame was entirely mine".
___E:McCain served as the Navy's liaison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_military_career_of_John_McCain#Senate_liaison,_divorce,_and_second_marriage)___ to the U.S.

Senate beginning in 1977.  In retrospect, he said that this represented his "real entry into the world of politics, and the beginning of my second career as a public servant."  His key behind-the-scenes role gained congressional financing for a new ___E:supercarrier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercarrier)___ against the wishes of the ___E:Carter administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carter_administration)___ .

In April 1979,  McCain met ___E:Cindy Lou Hensley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Lou_Hensley)___ , a teacher from ___E:Phoenix, Arizona U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix,_Arizona)___ , whose ___E:father U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Hensley)___ had founded ___E:a large beer distributorship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hensley_%26_Co.)___ .

They began dating, and he urged his wife, Carol, to grant him a divorce, which she did in February 1980; the uncontested divorce took effect in April 1980.   The settlement included two houses and financial support for her ongoing medical treatments due to her 1969 car accident; they remained on good terms.

McCain and Hensley were married on May 17, 1980, with Senators ___E:William Cohen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Cohen)___ and ___E:Gary Hart U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Hart)___ attending as ___E:groomsmen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groomsmen)___ .
McCain's children did not attend, and several years passed before they reconciled.

John and Cindy McCain entered into a ___E:prenuptial agreement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prenuptial_agreement)___ that kept most of her family's assets under her name; they kept their finances separate and filed separate ___E:income tax returns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_return_(United_States))___ .

McCain decided to leave the Navy. It was doubtful whether he would ever be promoted to the rank of ___E:full admiral U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admiral_(United_States))___ , as he had poor annual physicals and had not been given a major sea command.

His chances of being promoted to ___E:rear admiral U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rear_admiral_(lower_half))___ were better, but he declined that prospect, as he had already made plans to run for Congress and said he could "do more good there."

McCain retired from the Navy as a ___E:captain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(United_States_O-6))___ on April 1, 1981.   He was designated as disabled and awarded a ___E:disability pension U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veteran%27s_pension)___ .
Upon leaving the military, he moved to Arizona.

His numerous military decorations and awards include: the ___E:Silver Star U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Star)___ , two ___E:Legion of Merits U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legion_of_Merit)___ , ___E:Distinguished Flying Cross U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distinguished_Flying_Cross_(United_States))___ , three Bronze Star Medals, two ___E:Purple Hearts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purple_Heart)___ , two ___E:Navy and Marine Corps Commendation Medals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_and_Marine_Corps_Commendation_Medal)___ , and the ___E:Prisoner of War Medal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner_of_War_Medal)___ .

___E:McCain set his sights on becoming a representative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_House_and_Senate_career_of_John_McCain_(until_2000)#U.S._Congressman)___ because he was interested in current events, was ready for a new challenge, and had developed political ambitions.
Living in Phoenix, he went to work for his new father-in-law's large ___E:Anheuser-Busch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anheuser-Busch)___ beer distributorship.

As vice president of public relations at the distributorship, he gained political support among the local business community, meeting powerful figures such as banker ___E:Charles Keating Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Keating_Jr.)___ , real estate developer ___E:Fife Symington III U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fife_Symington_III)___ (later Governor of Arizona) and newspaper publisher ___E:Darrow "Duke" Tully U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darrow_%22Duke%22_Tully)___ .

In 1982, McCain ran as a Republican for an open seat in ___E:Arizona's 1st congressional district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona%27s_1st_congressional_district)___ , which was being vacated by 30-year incumbent Republican ___E:John Jacob Rhodes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jacob_Rhodes)___ .
A newcomer to the state, McCain was termed a ___E:carpetbagger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpetbagger)___ .
McCain responded to a voter making that charge with what a Phoenix Gazette columnist later described as "the most devastating response to a potentially troublesome political issue I've ever heard":

Listen, pal. I spent 22 years in the Navy. My father was in the Navy. My grandfather was in the Navy. We in the military service tend to move a lot. We have to live in all parts of the country, all parts of the world.
I wish I could have had the luxury, like you, of growing up and living and spending my entire life in a nice place like the First District of Arizona, but I was doing other things.
As a matter of fact, when I think about it now, the place I lived longest in my life was Hanoi.

McCain won a highly contested primary election with the assistance of local political endorsements, his ___E:Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C.)___ connections, and money that his wife lent to his campaign.
He then easily won the general election in the heavily Republican district.

In 1983, McCain was elected to lead the incoming group of Republican representatives,  and was assigned to the ___E:House Committee on Interior Affairs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Natural_Resources)___ .

Also that year, he opposed creation of a federal ___E:Martin Luther King Jr. Day U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr._Day)___ , but admitted in 2008: "I was wrong and eventually realized that, in time to give full support [in 1990] for a state holiday in Arizona."

At this point, McCain's politics were mainly in line with those of President ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ ; this included support for ___E:Reaganomics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reaganomics)___ , and he was active on Indian Affairs bills.
